[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.43.0 - the turret ring[/b][/size]

There's a hidden room under DaVinci's workshop. In it are his war machines — a catapult, a bladed
thing he calls the Sweeper, and a siege tank — and if you examine any of them the game tells you
the same thing: [b]it isn't finished.[/b]

He'll explain why. The machines need a spirit to turn their gears, and he thinks he knows where to
find one. That part of the story works; it sends you off on a real quest for a spirit gem.

The other half of the machine is gears. [b]Nobody in the original game ever asks about the gears[/b],
and the quest file for them was empty.

[b]Not the blacksmith[/b]

My first attempt at this sent you to Eduardo the smith. It was wrong twice over, and the second
reason is the interesting one: [b]gears in this game don't come from a blacksmith.[/b] They come from
DaVinci's talking steam engine, which already sells them.

It's in the workshop, it's enormous, it's rude, and if you pull its lever it says:

[i]*"So, he's too afraid to deal with me so he sends his apprentice? Very well, I'll make the gears,[/i]
[i]if you can provide me with a magical potion — any potion will do — so that I can create enchanted[/i]
[i]steam."*[/i]

That's how you get the crossbow gears in the original game. It's the gear-maker. It charges.

[b]Three ways to pay it[/b]

The turret ring is the big one — forty-one teeth, and it will tell you at length that it's the only
thing in Barcelona that can cut it.

- [b]Give it a potion.[/b] Costs you the potion.
- [b]Out-argue it.[/b] With enough Barter you can point out that something that rare doesn't haggle.
  It concedes, and resents you for it.
- [b]Promise it something it wants more than payment.[/b]

[b]The third one[/b]

The engine has a grievance, and it's in the original game, fully written:

[i]*"He [b]never[/b] gives credit where credit is due. [b]I[/b] am the brains behind this operation. I've[/i]
[i]helped him build all of his inventions, but what thanks do I receive? Just more work, and the[/i]
[i]occasional lubing."*[/i]

So it will cut the ring for free. What it wants is to hear you tell the old man, out loud, who made
it.

[i]*"Do not say it again to me, say it to him, [b]in this room[/b], out loud, where I can hear it and he[/i]
[i]cannot pretend he misheard. Thirty years of his drawings and my teeth and his name on all of it.[/i]
[i]I am not going anywhere, apprentice. I will be right here, waiting to hear it."*[/i]

[b]And then the quest ends without you doing it.[/b] You carry the gear down to the chamber, DaVinci
fits it, thanks you, pays you, and the journal closes. The engine is still owed.

You can settle it later, upstairs, where it can actually hear you. Or you can not. [b]There is no
option anywhere to deliberately break the promise[/b] — you just never go back, which is how this
kind of promise actually gets broken. The engine will keep bringing it up:

[i]*"I cut it. You carried it up the stairs and he put his hands on it and I have not heard one word[/i]
[i]since. He is in this room most evenings, apprentice. I am not asking you to write it on the[/i]
[i]cathedral. One sentence, where I can hear it."*[/i]

If you do say it, DaVinci doesn't get angry. He gets embarrassed.

[i]*"...It said that to you. Out loud. To a stranger. Forgive me, I am laughing at myself and not at[/i]
[i]you — it is right, of course. It has been right for thirty years and I have been too proud and too[/i]
[i]busy to walk ten feet and say so."*[/i]

Nothing mechanical rewards keeping it. That's deliberate.

[b]Installing[/b]

Unzip and double-click [b][i]Mod Manager.bat[/i][/b], then click the button that names the mod.

Works on [b]any save[/b]. You'll need to have found the hidden chamber for DaVinci to raise the gears
at all.

[b]If you play it[/b]

[b]The check that matters:[/b] take the promise route, hand over the gear, let the quest close, then go
back up to the workshop. The engine must still be owed, and DaVinci must still have an option to
hear it. If the debt vanishes when the quest completes, the whole point of the release is gone.

[b]And the honest question:[/b] does keeping it feel worth doing when there's no reward for it? If the
answer is no, I'd rather know — that's the only thing this release is really trying to do.
